introduction.title: Introduction
paragraphs: I’m Ivan Fulvian Pitoyo, a Biomedical Engineering graduate passionate about building technology that connects engineering, artificial intelligence, and healthcare. My interests lie in Computer Vision, Biomedical Instrumentation, Embedded Systems, and Medical Device Engineering.

During my undergraduate studies, I developed projects ranging from AI-based malaria parasite detection using YOLOv8m to an ESP32-based Smart Glove for speech-impaired users. These experiences allowed me to work across software, hardware, data analysis, prototyping, and system testing.

Alongside my technical work, I have also developed my leadership and teamwork skills through organizational roles, laboratory supervision, and project coordination. I am eager to continue developing my skills and contribute to the medical device and healthcare technology industry through engineering and innovation.

education.title: My Education
education.imageAlt: Aerial view of Institut Teknologi Sumatera campus
education.paragraph: I completed my Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical Engineering at Institut Teknologi Sumatera (ITERA). During my undergraduate studies, I explored the intersection of engineering, technology, and healthcare through laboratory work, technical projects, and research. My academic interests developed around Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, Biomedical Instrumentation, Medical Imaging, Biosensors, and Embedded Systems, leading me to work on projects such as an ESP32-based Smart Glove and a YOLOv8m-based malaria parasite detection system.

card.detail: Focused on the application of engineering and technology in healthcare, with academic and project experience in Computer Vision, Biomedical Instrumentation, Embedded Systems, Biosensors, and Medical Image Processing.

list.title: Smart Glove for Speech-Impaired Users
list.summary: A wearable ESP32-based glove that translates hand gestures into real-time speech and text output.
list.imageAlt: Team presenting the Smart Glove at the BIONE exhibition
paragraphs: This project developed a wearable Smart Glove for speech-impaired users to translate hand gestures into real-time outputs. The system combines an ESP32, flex sensors, an MPU-6050 IMU, Bluetooth communication, embedded programming, and an Android interface.
list.detailNote: The resulting prototype successfully recognized 5 hand gestures with 92% average accuracy and operated continuously for 6 hours and 42 minutes.

list.title: Undergraduate Thesis: YOLOv8m-Based Malaria Parasite Detection
list.summary: An AI system for detecting malaria parasites in microscopic blood-smear images in real time.
list.imageAlt: Laboratory setup used for the malaria detection thesis
paragraphs: This project focused on developing an AI-based system for detecting malaria parasites in microscopic blood-smear images using a fine-tuned YOLOv8m model. The study involved image preprocessing, data augmentation, class-imbalance handling, and hyperparameter optimization using Optuna.
list.detailNote: The final model was integrated into a Python and OpenCV-based GUI for real-time detection using a microscope camera.
